insights.topic: Verified purchase data vs. probabilistic targeting
insights.insight: Crinkl's cryptographically verified receipts confirm purchases happened — not inferred from browsing behavior. At $5+ CPM for probabilistic signals, the gap between inference and proof represents the addressable premium for deterministic commerce data.

insights.topic: Grocery dominance with high-value unknown category
insights.insight: Grocery-supermarkets leads the 14-day category mix at 28.4% of receipts ($44.44 average ticket), but the Unknown category averages $89.18 per receipt — double grocery — and has held that premium across every observed snapshot, suggesting a high-spend segment that has not yet been classified and may reward early investigation.

insights.topic: Cycle ceiling compression after record highs
insights.insight: The 7-day GMV cycle peaked at an all-time high of $91,360 on Nov 19, then stepped down to $75,349 on Nov 20 and $65,614 on Nov 21 — two consecutive declining peaks after two weeks of expansion. Brands evaluating reach trajectory should note the ceiling is compressing even as the floor also sets new lows.

insights.topic: Floor regression diverging from ceiling behavior
insights.insight: Post-rolloff trough GMV has declined on back-to-back cycles — $64,842 on Nov 20 and $60,995 on Nov 21 — while the cycle ceiling has also pulled back from its record. Floors and ceilings are moving together downward now, which is a different regime than the expansion phase that ran through Nov 19.

insights.topic: Restaurants & Dining category now structurally confirmed
insights.insight: Restaurants & Dining first appeared in the 14-day trailing aggregate on Nov 20 and has stabilized at 810 receipts and $24,762 in GMV — it is not a data artifact. For QSR and casual dining brands, this confirms a verified, receipt-level purchase signal exists in the feed.

insights.topic: Geographic diffusion expanding the addressable footprint
insights.insight: New CBSA codes are entering the visible dataset on a rolling basis — CBSA 22220 became observable as recently as Nov 20 — indicating that receipt capture is spreading into new metro areas, which matters for brands assessing whether regional or national targeting is viable against this data source.
